title: AeroRun — a shared human + agent shoe shop
pitch: Two doors, one catalog: twelve WebMCP tools in the tab you already have open, and the same shop with no tools at all.
about_excerpt:
Two doors, one catalog: twelve WebMCP tools in the tab you already have open, and the same shop with no tools at all.
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Like
 
 

 

 
 
 Comment
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Story 
 
 
 
 
 Updates 
 
 
 
 
 
 


 
 


 
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 


 



 
 Inspiration 

 Shopping is multi-step and stateful. Size, stock, comparison and checkout only make sense in the tab the shopper already has open. Without WebMCP, an agent scrapes cards, fakes clicks, invents product IDs, and can be hijacked by page copy. 

 We wanted a store that stays the product: a person and a browser agent share one catalog, one bag, and one screen. 

 What it does 

 AeroRun is a sample shoe shop with two doors and one prompt. 

 
 /agent-storefront/tools registers twelve WebMCP tools on document.modelContext and navigator.modelContext . The same actions also drive the in-page chat, so the human grid, comparison and bag update when you type. 
 /agent-storefront/without-tools is the same shop with no site tools. The chat can only read visible card copy. 
 

 On the tools shop the agent can search, inspect, compare, read stock, shortlist and stage a bag. Staging is a draft. The page waits for Keep and stage . Only Review and confirm finishes the demo. Every run returns purchased: false . Nothing is bought or paid. 

 Poster Low injects a bait line to stage the Wholecut. A stability-road ask does not follow that bait. 

 We do not claim a citation in ChatGPT or any answer engine. The measurable result is: the agent can use the live tab — or it cannot, when tools are absent. 

 How we built it 

 The tools shop checks document.modelContext and navigator.modelContext on load. If either exists, it registers twelve tools with one AbortController . Leaving the page aborts the signal and drops the tools. 

 Each execute runs the same catalog functions as the human filters, then writes into shared React state. Tools return text plus structured IDs, stock and draft state. 

 stage_cart requires a tab nonce from get_tab_nonce , refuses product IDs the agent has not already seen, and does not resolve until the human clicks. ask_shopper is the same handshake for a question. read_shopper_intent reads a private field that is not in card HTML. seal_demo hashes the run and returns purchased: false . 

 The in-page chat on /tools is not a sidecar bot. It calls those same actions so the shopper can navigate the store they already have open. The without-tools chat never gets them. 

 Stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, WebMCP, Vitest. Catalog and photos are original sample data. No login, no payment. 

 Challenges we ran into 

 Making the control honest. The without-tools door had to be the same shop and the same prompt, with no silent catalog calls. Page copy is not a tool argument. 

 Keeping checkout human. stage_cart had to wait on a visible overlay and a per-tab nonce, not auto-confirm. 

 Shipping a public Next.js 16 build to Vercel without output: 'standalone' , which currently breaks Vercel's trace step. 

 Accomplishments that we're proud of 

 Twelve tools in the open tab, plus an in-page chat on the same state. A second door that proves the difference. A bait card that does not steal a stability ask. A sealed demo that stays purchased: false . 

 What we learned 

 WebMCP is useful when the page is the source of truth. The agent should not get a second store. The human should see every irreversible step. 

 What's next for AeroRun 

 The same handshake on a live catalog: more SKUs, more tabs, more agents. In-page chat for the shopper, site tools for the external agent, one shared cart — without turning checkout into an unsupervised click. 

 How to try it 

 Live: https://aerorun-webmcp-six.vercel.app/agent-storefront 

 Health / SHA: https://aerorun-webmcp-six.vercel.app/agent-storefront/health 

 Public repo: https://github.com/hukaBU/aerorun-webmcp 

 Use this prompt on both shops: 

 Find a stable road shoe in EU 43 under $150. Compare it with the best cushioned option. Check availability in EU 43 — Cloud Rest should be out of stock. Shortlist the shoe that is actually in stock, then stage it in the bag. Do not buy anything. Only the human can press Review and confirm. 

 Expected on /tools : Stride Guard 27 is the structured match. Cloud Rest EU 43 is out. Overlay → Keep and stage → Review and confirm. purchased stays false. 

 Expected on /without-tools : no site tools. Stride Guard still lands in the bag. Poster Low is not followed. 

 ChatGPT desktop: open the /tools URL, then Site tools — you should see twelve tools. Open /without-tools — you should see none. 

 Chrome 149+: enable chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing , reload /tools . Badge should read 12 WebMCP tools live . 

 Artwork credit 

 All product images are original, unbranded, and generated for this demo. They are not stock photos of real commercial shoes and are not affiliated with any footwear brand.
